_comment_family: Syne ships as a family - an Extra, a Bold, a Semi Bold and a Regular
- and every one of those files carries 'Syne' as name ID 1, with the
cut in the subfamily. The Bold is already in this folder, brought in
as re-belle's highlight, so the danger here is not theoretical: a
request for 'Syne' alone would be the same request the Bold answers,
and a machine with that cut installed would set a whole block of
So the full name (name ID 4) is what gets declared, exactly as
syne-bold.json declares 'Syne Bold' and the two Telegraf packs
declare theirs. The PostScript name spells the same cut with a
hyphen, and both spellings are listed in `local` below rather than
one of them being tidied into the other.
Weight 400, which is the file's own usWeightClass and what the cut is
called. It is a static instance cut out of a variable family - there
is no fvar table in this file - so there is no axis here for a 400 to
be interpolated along and nothing for a browser to synthesise.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON at load time (see registerFace in
js/channels.js), which is the route content/README.md describes.
Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file,
and used by the installer as the name it registers this face under
The PostScript name first, then the Windows full name. Both name this
one cut rather than the family, so a machine answering to either is
answering with this file - which is exactly what the fallback route
is for. 'Syne' on its own is deliberately absent, for the reason
above: it is the name every other weight of the family answers to,
the Bold this app also ships included.
_comment_stack: Damage limitation, never a design choice - a block laid out against
the wrong metrics is broken rather than merely different, which is
what fontguard exists to catch before anything is drawn.
Chosen all the same, and the one thing it must not do is end up
anywhere near the face used beside it. This is a BLOCK face on a
channel whose highlight is Bebas Neue (see beauty-tipps), so the two
stacks are written as opposites: bebas-neue falls through Anton and
Impact - a condensed display face, then the nearest thing Windows can
be relied on to have - and this one falls through Segoe UI and Arial.
Whatever a machine is missing, the picked word stays the tall
condensed one and the block stays the ordinary-width grotesque.
Impact and Arial Black are absent on purpose, the same way they are
in syne-bold.json. Syne Regular is a display grotesque at a text
weight, so a substitute far heavier and much narrower than it would
not merely look different - on this channel it would land in the same
register as the highlight and take the difference between them away.
